correctness.rationale: For fixed diagonal pairs c(i)=(a_i,b_i), the bracket on an arrow corner is (a_i−a_j)v_ij−(b_i−b_j)u_ij. Diagonal and loop output vanish; each off-diagonal corner is in the bracket span by [e_i,u]=u. Unequal colors give a surjective linear map with q^dimension preimages per target; equal colors give q^(2 dimension) for zero only. Multiplying gives the claimed q^(2h+M) normalization and support-conditioned weights. Exact support F gives product over its edges of (q^μ−1) possible targets, subject to q²-colorability for a single bracket. For r brackets, the tuple of r diagonal pairs must separate every edge supporting the sum. Conversely use a proper q^(2r)-coloring, route each nonzero edge vector entirely to one separating coordinate pair, and solve the independent corner equations. The argument includes r=0, the zero target, no off-diagonal arrows, both orientations and characteristic two. A full-support target attains the maximum.
residual_risks: Only split radical-square-zero path quotients are covered. The bounded spot checks do not establish large-width bounds; those follow from the exact coloring construction.

value.rationale: A support graph gives an exact length for each bracket target and sharp worst cases that are unbounded at fixed field size. This also identifies all unattainable single brackets, with precise fiber multiplicities for the remaining targets, substantially beyond an average commutativity statistic.
residual_risks: The exact classification does not make chromatic number computationally easy.
